paragraphs.text: More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work

sentences.text: More fathers are taking paternity leave, but mothers are still doing all the work

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.translationLiteral: 越来越多的父亲在休陪产假，但母亲仍然承担着所有的活儿。
analysis.translationNatural: 当爹的休陪产假越来越普遍，可家里的活还是当妈的全包。
analysis.structMarkup: {More fathers} _are taking_ ~paternity leave~, {but} {mothers} _are still doing_ ~all the work~.
analysis.structureSummary: 两个并列分句（but 转折）：主谓宾 + 主谓宾

components.part: are still doing all the work

clauses: but 连接两个并列分句，形成“表面进步、实质未变”的对照。
全句为标题式表达，省略了冠词等成分。

phrases.usage: paternity 父亲；对应 maternity leave（产假）。
phrases.example: He took two weeks of paternity leave. 他休了两周陪产假。

phrases.usage: 此处既指家务也指育儿，语气略带讽刺。
phrases.example: She does all the work and gets no credit. 活都是她干的，功劳却没有。

pitfalls: paternity（父亲的）与 maternity（母亲的）别混。
are taking / are doing 用进行时，强调趋势与现状。
analysis.paragraphRole: 以标题式判断开篇，点出全文张力：观念在变，但分工没变。

paragraphs.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

sentences.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

analysis.senseInContext: 父亲的、父职的（paternity leave 陪产假）
examples: He took paternity leave after the birth. 孩子出生后他休了陪产假。

more.confusables: paternity 父亲的 / maternity 母亲的；paternal 慈父般的

analysis.senseInContext: 偏见（gender bias persists 性别偏见依然存在）
examples: The study found bias in hiring. 研究发现招聘中存在偏见。

more.roots: 源自古法语 biais（斜的）→ 倾斜 → 偏向
more.confusables: bias 可指“偏差/偏好”；prejudice 贬义更重

analysis.translationLiteral: 根据一项针对职场父母的新研究，过去五年美国对陪产假的态度发生了剧烈变化，因为更多父亲愿意休较长假，但在职业前景和家庭方面，性别偏见依然存在。
analysis.translationNatural: 一项针对职场父母的新研究显示：过去五年美国人对陪产假的态度变化很大，越来越多父亲愿意休长假；但在职业前途与家庭分工上，性别偏见依旧。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Attitudes (towards paternity leave)】 _have drastically changed_ (in America) (in the last five years) {as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off}, {but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home}, (according to a new study of working parents).
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + as 原因状语从句 + but 并列分句 + according to 状语

components.note: 现在完成时，drastically 表程度

components.part: as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off
when it comes to career prospects and the home
components.note: when it comes to 是固定说法

components.part: according to a new study of working parents

clauses: as 引导原因状语从句（此处表“因为”，不是“当……时”）。
but 连接转折分句。
when it comes to... 是固定表达，后接名词。

phrases.meaning: 做某事感到自在/愿意做
phrases.usage: 后接动名词；comfortable 表心理上的接受。
phrases.example: She feels comfortable speaking in public. 她不怵当众讲话。

phrases.usage: extended time off 指“较长的假期”。
phrases.example: He took a month off work. 他休了一个月假。
When it comes to price, they win. 论价格，他们占优。

pitfalls: as 在此表原因，不是“当……时”。
feel comfortable taking：后接动名词。
persists（仍然存在）主语是 gender bias，用单数。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出全文核心判断：态度变了，但偏见未消。

paragraphs.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

sentences.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

analysis.translationLiteral: 波士顿学院工作与家庭中心的研究调查了四家美国大公司中有资格享受至少六周带薪育儿假的新父母，发现接受调查的 1240 名员工中有 81% 表示，父亲休假的观念已变得更容易被接受。
analysis.translationNatural: 波士顿学院“工作与家庭中心”调查了四家美国大公司里符合条件（至少六周带薪育儿假）的新手父母：1240 名受访员工中，81% 认为“父亲休假”这件事已经更容易被接受。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Research (by the Boston College Center for Work & Family), {which surveyed new parents at four large US companies {who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave}},】 _found_ ~{that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主语（带两层定语从句）+ 谓语 + 宾语从句（内含第二层宾语从句）

components.part: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family
which surveyed new parents at four large US companies
who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave
that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said...
the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable

clauses: which surveyed... 是非限制性定语从句，修饰 research。
who were qualified for... 是定语从句，修饰 new parents。
that 81% of... said... 是宾语从句，作 found 的宾语。
the notion of... has become more acceptable 是省略 that 的宾语从句，作 said 的宾语。

phrases.usage: 后接名词或动名词；qualification 是名词。
phrases.example: She is qualified for the position. 她符合这个职位的资格。

phrases.usage: parental 父母的；paid 带薪的。
phrases.example: The company offers 12 weeks paid parental leave. 公司提供 12 周带薪育儿假。
The notion of working from home is now normal. 在家办公这一观念如今很常见。

pitfalls: 两层定语从句套在主语上，找主干时先抓 Research ... found that...。
employees surveyed 中 surveyed 是过去分词作后置定语。
the notion of fathers taking leave：of + 动名词复合结构。
analysis.paragraphRole: 给出调查数据：81% 认为父亲休假已被接受，支撑“态度变化”。

paragraphs.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

sentences.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

analysis.translationLiteral: 在受访者中，62% 的父亲休了最长假期，而母亲为 93%；约四分之三的员工表示雇主对父母双方休育儿假的支持是同等的，过半员工表示休假政策改善了职场文化。
analysis.translationNatural: 受访者里，62% 的父亲休满了最长假期，母亲则是 93%；约四分之三的人说公司对爸妈休育儿假的支持一样，超过一半的人说这些政策让职场文化变好了。
analysis.structMarkup: 【62% of fathers】 _took_ ~the maximum amount of time off~ (compared to 93% of mothers), {and} 【around three-quarters of workers】 _said_ ~{their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave}~ {and} 【over half】 _said_ ~{leave policies had made workplace culture better}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 三个并列分句：主谓宾 + 主谓宾从句 + 主谓宾从句

components.part: took the maximum amount of time off
their employer was equally supportive of...
leave policies had made workplace culture better
components.note: said 的宾语，用过去完成时

clauses: 三个分句由 and 连接，都是调查数据。
said 后省略 that，接宾语从句。
had made 用过去完成时，表示政策生效在“说”之前。

phrases.example: Compared to last year, sales doubled. 与去年相比销量翻倍。

phrases.usage: 形容词 supportive + of；动词 support。
phrases.example: Managers should be supportive of new ideas. 管理者应支持新想法。

phrases.usage: maximum 作形容词；反义 minimum。
phrases.example: Use the maximum amount of time allowed. 用足允许的最大时间。

pitfalls: 62% of fathers 作主语，谓语用复数 took。
equally supportive of mothers and fathers：equally 修饰 supportive。
had made 是过去完成时（政策效果先于受访者的评价）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用具体比例对照（62% vs 93%），揭示“父亲休假仍少于母亲”的现实。

paragraphs.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

sentences.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue.

analysis.senseInContext: 法定的（statutory paid leave 法定带薪假）
examples: Employees have statutory rights. 员工享有法定权利。

more.confusables: statutory 法定的；statuary 是“雕像”，拼写相近

analysis.translationLiteral: 美国是世界上仅有的三个不提供法定带薪假期的国家之一，但越来越多的州和公司开始着手解决这个问题。
analysis.translationNatural: 全球只有三个国家没有法定带薪假，美国是其中之一；不过越来越多的州和企业已经开始动手解决这事。
analysis.structMarkup: 【The US】 _is_ ~one of only three countries (in the world) (not to offer statutory paid leave)~, {but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue}.
analysis.structureSummary: 主系表（one of + 复数）+ but 并列分句

components.part: not to offer statutory paid leave
but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue
components.note: 转折：州与企业开始行动

clauses: one of + 复数名词作表语，谓语用单数 is。
but 连接转折分句。
take up 表示“着手处理”。

phrases.usage: statutory 法定的；statute 是法规。
phrases.example: Statutory holidays differ by country. 法定假日各国不同。

phrases.usage: take up 表“开始从事、接手”。
phrases.example: The committee took up the issue last week. 委员会上周着手处理该问题。

pitfalls: one of only three countries：谓语用单数 is。
not to offer... 是不定式作后置定语，修饰 countries。
take up 与 take on、take over 含义不同（此处为“着手处理”）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 指出制度背景：美国缺乏法定带薪假，但情况正在变化。

sentences.text: So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

analysis.translationLiteral: 到目前为止，八个州和哥伦比亚特区有自己的带薪家事假法律。
analysis.translationNatural: 到目前为止，已有八个州和哥伦比亚特区出台了带薪家事假法。
analysis.structMarkup: (So far), 【eight states and the District of Columbia】 _have_ ~their own paid family leave laws~.

components.note: 到目前为止（常配现在完成时）

components.part: eight states and the District of Columbia
components.note: 八个州 + 哥伦比亚特区（并列）

components.part: their own paid family leave laws

clauses: 本句是简单句，没有从句。

phrases.example: So far, no one has complained. 到目前为止没人抱怨。

phrases.usage: 比 parental leave 范围更广。
phrases.example: Paid family leave helps new parents. 带薪家事假帮助新手父母。

pitfalls: so far 常配现在完成时（但此处 have 表状态）。
the District of Columbia 指华盛顿特区，不是“哥伦比亚国家”。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用具体数字说明制度层面的进展。

paragraphs.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

sentences.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave.

analysis.translationLiteral: 该中心的执行主任、这项研究的主要作者 Brad Harrington 估计，美国只有 20% 到 30% 的公司提供带薪育儿假。
analysis.translationNatural: 该中心执行主任、本研究第一作者 Brad Harrington 估计：全美只有 20% 到 30% 的公司提供带薪育儿假。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Brad Harrington, (executive director of the center) and (lead author of the study),】 _estimates_ ~{only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主语（带同位语）+ 谓语 + 宾语从句（省略 that）

components.part: executive director of the center and lead author of the study
only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave

clauses: estimates 后省略 that，引导宾语从句。
executive director of the center and lead author of the study 是同位语，解释 Brad Harrington 的身份。

phrases.usage: 机构职务名；director 董事/主任。
phrases.example: She is the executive director of the foundation. 她是该基金会的执行主任。

phrases.usage: 学术语境；对应 co-author（合著者）。
phrases.example: The lead author presented the findings. 第一作者介绍了研究结果。

pitfalls: estimates 后省略 that。
20% to 30% of companies 作从句主语，谓语用复数 offer。
analysis.paragraphRole: 用专家估算给出覆盖率现实：多数公司并没有这项福利。

sentences.text: He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

analysis.translationLiteral: 他认为这些研究结果反映了企业对新父亲休假态度的明显变化。
analysis.translationNatural: 他觉得这些发现说明：企业对“新爸爸休假”的态度确实有了明显转变。
analysis.structMarkup: 【He】 _feels_ ~{the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off}~.
analysis.structureSummary: 主谓 + 宾语从句（省略 that）

components.part: the research findings reflect an obvious change
in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off

clauses: feels 后省略 that，接宾语从句。
to new fathers taking time off 是介词短语，其中 taking time off 是动名词复合结构。

phrases.example: The data reflects a shift in habits. 数据反映出习惯的转变。
Corporate attitudes to remote work vary. 企业对远程办公的态度各异。

pitfalls: feel 在此是“认为”，不是“感觉”。
attitudes to 后接动名词复合结构 new fathers taking time off。
analysis.paragraphRole: 引用专家判断，收束“态度确实在变”这一层意思。

paragraphs.text: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

paragraphs.text: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.

paragraphs.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

sentences.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

paragraphs.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.

sentences.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner.
But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture.
While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it.
A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.

paragraphs.text: Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.

paragraphs.text: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.

paragraphs.text: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'"

paragraphs.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

sentences.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave.
Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers.
Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave.
Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

paragraphs.text: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.

paragraphs.text: "I do think there's still some way to go...there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change." He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time."

questions.stem: In the absence of Federal legislation, some states in the US have passed laws concerning paid family leave.
Most fathers admitted that even during their paternity leave they actually did much less childcare than the mother.
According to one father, equal parental leave is indispensable to achieving gender equality in the workplace.
One survey indicated there is now less objection to paternity leave.
Compared to five years ago, according to one researcher, many more people said their organisation gave the same support to men and women taking parental leave.
One study finds that even workers who claim to desire gender equality stick to traditional gender roles both at work and at home.
The majority of workers surveyed said parental leave policies had improved workplace culture.
In spite of progress, the number of women in top positions of big companies remains extremely small.
According to one estimate, less than one third of companies in the US provide paid parental leave.
A number of lawsuits have pressured companies to formulate gender neutral policies on parental leave.
